guitar.evidence: Brian May's homemade "Red Special" guitar is one of the most iconic and well-documented instruments in rock history.

tone.target: bright Queen pop-rock crunch with chime and layered space
tone.profile: bright Queen pop-rock crunch with chime and layered space
tone.summary: A classic pop-rock chain utilizing a Fender/British clean amp model (US Deluxe or AC30 TB), light OD boost for crunch, Chorus for shimmer, and Plate Reverb for space.

rig.name: Queen - Somebody To Love - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide light, chimey crunch and upper-mid punch (AC30 style).
blocks.gap: The Green OD is a good proxy for the desired 'Brit chime' boost.

blocks.purpose: Bypass or use a clean boost if needed; keeping the gain light.
blocks.gap: No dedicated distortion unit is required as the Green OD provides sufficient crunch.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the bright, chimey British clean headroom required for Queen's pop-rock sound.
Provide a classic British cabinet voicing that complements the AC30 tone.
blocks.gap: The UK Vintage 4x12 is a solid choice for pop-rock, though US 2x12 might be considered if pure Fender chime was prioritized.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle shimmer and width to the tone, fulfilling the 'subtle modulation' requirement.
Enhance the upper mids and brightness (jangly upper mids) while controlling low-end mud.
Add layered space and shimmer without sounding overly wet or dark.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the UK 4x12 for a more open/American voicing IR.

proposals.reason: Better captures the bright, articulate Fender-style chime needed for Queen's pop sound.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and openness in upper mids/treble.
